caption: Ahead only
colour: blue circle, white upward arrow
explanation: You must continue straight ahead in the direction of the arrow; turning is not permitted here. Keep moving forward and do not turn off.
mnemonic: Blue means do; arrow up means go straight through.
notes: Commons description: 'Go straight ahead only.' Diagram 606 (ahead variant); blue circle with white up arrow. Verified file page exists.

caption: Turn left ahead
colour: blue circle, white arrow angled up-left
explanation: You must turn left at the junction ahead; the angled arrow warns the turn is coming up. Prepare to turn left.
mnemonic: Arrow leaning forward-left = the left turn is just ahead.
notes: Commons description: 'Turn left ahead.' Diagram 609; blue circle, white arrow pointing up and to the left. Verified.

caption: Turn right ahead
colour: blue circle, white arrow angled up-right
explanation: You must turn right at the junction ahead; the angled arrow warns the turn is coming up. Prepare to turn right.
mnemonic: Arrow leaning forward-right = the right turn is just ahead.
notes: Commons description: 'Turn right ahead.' Diagram 609 (right variant); blue circle, white arrow up and to the right. Verified.

caption: Keep left
colour: blue circle, white arrow pointing left
explanation: You must pass to the left of the sign, for example at a central island or obstruction. Keep to the left-hand side.
mnemonic: Horizontal arrow = pass that side now (left), not a turn ahead.
notes: Commons description: 'Keep left.' Diagram 610; blue circle, white horizontal arrow pointing left. Verified. Often mounted on keep-left bollards.

caption: Keep right
colour: blue circle, white arrow pointing right
explanation: You must pass to the right of the sign, for example at a central island or obstruction. Keep to the right-hand side.
mnemonic: Horizontal arrow = pass that side now (right), not a turn ahead.
notes: Commons description: 'Keep right.' Diagram 610 (right variant); blue circle, white horizontal arrow pointing right. Verified.

caption: Mini-roundabout
colour: blue circle, three white curved arrows clockwise
explanation: A mini-roundabout is ahead: give way to traffic coming from your right and go round it clockwise. Slow down and be ready to give way.
mnemonic: Round arrows = go round; always give way to the right.
notes: Commons description: 'Mini-roundabout (give way to traffic from the right and circulate clockwise).' Diagram 611.1; blue circle with three white clockwise arrows. Verified.

caption: Pass either side
colour: blue circle, two white arrows up-left and up-right
explanation: You may pass on either side of the obstruction or island ahead to reach the same destination. Choose a clear side and pass safely.
mnemonic: Two arrows splitting = take either side, they meet again.
notes: Commons description: 'Pass on either side (to reach the same destination).' Diagram 611; blue circle, two diverging white arrows. Verified.

caption: Route for pedal cycles only
colour: blue circle, white bicycle
explanation: This route is for pedal cycles only; motor vehicles must not use it. As a rider, do not enter on your motorcycle.
mnemonic: Blue circle, bike only = pedal power, no engines.
notes: Commons description: 'Route for use by pedal cycles only.' Diagram 955; blue circle, white bicycle. Verified. (Note: triangular 950 is the cycle-route warning, not this.)

caption: Turn left at junction
colour: blue circle, white arrow pointing left
explanation: At the junction you must turn left; the horizontal arrow shows the turn is here, not further ahead. Turn left now.
mnemonic: Flat arrow = turn here; angled arrow (609) = ahead.
notes: Commons description: 'Turn left.' Diagram 606 (left variant); blue circle, white horizontal arrow pointing left. Verified. Distinct from 609 'turn left ahead' (angled arrow).

caption: Segregated pedal cycle and pedestrian route
colour: blue circle, bicycle and pedestrian split by white vertical line
explanation: A shared route where cyclists and pedestrians have separate sides divided by a line; each must keep to their own side. Motor vehicles must not enter.
mnemonic: Line down the middle = stay in your lane, segregated.
notes: Commons description: 'Route for segregated use by pedal cycles and pedestrians only.' Diagram 957; blue circle, bicycle and pedestrian separated by a vertical white line. Verified.

caption: Shared cycle and pedestrian route
colour: blue circle, bicycle above pedestrian, no dividing line
explanation: A route shared by cyclists and pedestrians with no separation; both use the same space, so cyclists must give way considerately. Motor vehicles must not enter.
mnemonic: No line = shared space, watch out for each other.
notes: Commons description: 'Route for shared use by pedal cycles and pedestrians only.' Diagram 956; blue circle, bicycle and pedestrian with no dividing line. Verified.

caption: Minimum speed
colour: blue circle, white number (e.g. 30)
explanation: You must not drive slower than the speed shown unless conditions make it unsafe. Keep your speed at or above this figure.
mnemonic: Blue = must do; so you must do at least this speed.
notes: Commons description: 'Minimum speed limit of 30 miles per hour (TSRGDNO 672).' Diagram 672; blue circle, white number. Verified. Number varies; 30 shown as the standard example.

caption: End of minimum speed
colour: blue circle, white number with red diagonal line
explanation: The minimum speed limit no longer applies from this point. You are free to travel below that figure if needed.
mnemonic: Red slash through it = that rule is now crossed out.
notes: Commons description: 'End of 30 miles per hour minimum speed limit (TSRGDNO 673).' Diagram 673; blue circle, white number with red diagonal bar. Verified.

caption: Buses and cycles only
colour: blue circle, white bus and white bicycle
explanation: This route is for buses and pedal cycles only; other motor vehicles must not use it. Do not enter on your motorcycle.
mnemonic: Bus + bike in blue = only these two belong.
notes: Commons description: 'Route for use by buses and cycles only (TSRGDNO 953).' Diagram 953; blue circle with white bus and bicycle symbols. Verified.

caption: Trams only
colour: blue circle, white tram
explanation: This route is for trams only; all other vehicles are prohibited. Never enter a tram-only route on your motorcycle.
mnemonic: Blue circle, tram only = rails, not road for you.
notes: Commons description: 'Route for use by tramcars only (TSRGDNO 953.1).' Diagram 953.1; blue circle, white tram. Verified. (953.2 is the explanatory plate, not this sign.)

caption: Contra-flow bus lane
colour: blue rectangle, white bus and upward arrow against traffic flow
explanation: Ahead, buses travel towards you in a lane running against the normal traffic flow; expect oncoming buses and do not enter that lane. Stay in your correct lane.
mnemonic: Contra = against; the bus arrow faces back at you.
notes: Commons description: 'Contra-flow bus lane (TSRGDNO 960).' Diagram 960; blue rectangular sign with white bus symbol and arrow indicating buses against the flow. Verified.

caption: With-flow bus lane
colour: blue rectangle, white bus, cycle (and 'taxi'), with operating times
explanation: A bus lane runs ahead in the same direction as the traffic flow, usually with a cycle (and sometimes taxi) symbol and its hours of operation; do not drive in it during those times. Stay in the general traffic lane.
mnemonic: With-flow = bus goes your way; check the times before using it.
notes: Diagram 958 (with-flow bus, cycle and taxi lane). Treated as composite: 'UK_traffic_sign_958.svg' returns HTTP 404 on Commons (no single canonical SVG) because the sign varies with vehicle symbols and an incorporated time-of-operation plate (diagram 961). Unverified; best-guess diagram 958 confirmed via TSRGD/Traffic Signs Manual references. 959.1 on Commons is the with-flow CYCLE lane, not this.

caption: Turn right at junction
colour: blue circle, white arrow pointing right
explanation: At the junction you must turn right; the horizontal arrow shows the turn is here, not further ahead. Turn right now.
mnemonic: Flat arrow = turn here; angled arrow (609) = ahead.
notes: Commons: 'Turn right.' Diagram 606 (right variant). Mirror of existing turn-left-at-junction (606 left).

caption: Buses and trams only
colour: blue circle, white bus and white tram
explanation: This route is for buses and trams only; other motor vehicles must not use it. Do not enter on your motorcycle.
mnemonic: Bus + tram in blue = only those two belong.
notes: Commons: 'Route for use by buses and tramcars only (TSRGDNO 953.1V)'. Distinct from 953 buses-and-cycles and 953.1 trams-only.

caption: Shared route for horses, cycles and pedestrians
colour: blue circle, white horse-and-rider, bicycle and pedestrian, no dividing line
explanation: A route shared by horse riders, cyclists and pedestrians with no separation between them; all use the same space, so give way considerately. Motor vehicles must not enter.
mnemonic: Horse, bike, walker together = share nicely, no line.
notes: Commons: 'Route for shared use by accompanied horses, pedal cycles and pedestrians only.' Diagram 956.1. Extends existing 956.

caption: With-flow cycle lane
colour: blue rectangle, white bicycle and upward arrow with the traffic flow
explanation: A cycle lane runs ahead in the same direction as the traffic flow; you must not drive or park in it during its hours of operation. Keep out of the marked cycle lane.
mnemonic: Bike + arrow your way = leave the cycle lane for cycles.
notes: Commons: 'With-flow cycle lane (TSRGDNO 959.1)'. Cycle counterpart to existing 958 with-flow bus lane.

caption: With-flow cycle lane ahead
colour: blue square, white bicycle, lane diagram and arrow with the traffic flow
explanation: Warns that a with-flow cycle lane begins on the road ahead; get ready to keep out of the cycle lane once it starts. Position yourself in the correct traffic lane.
mnemonic: Lane diagram = cycle lane is just ahead, stay out of it.
notes: Commons: 'With-flow cycle lane ahead (TSRGDNO 958.1)'. Advance version of 959.1.
